prize_parts.citation: for showing how population-scale administrative data can measure intergenerational mobility and identify the causal effects of place on children's outcomes

statement.case_for: My ballot and my names are unchanged from round 1. What has changed is how I weigh the risks and how explicitly I state the scope. B002 still seems to me the clearest case of measurement and identification done together. Linked population records let economists observe opportunity by place and group directly, instead of inferring it from small surveys. The causal strand (movers, exposure effects, re-analysis of an experiment) does not depend on the descriptive atlas. The two strands can therefore constrain each other, and that triangulation is the main reason I trust the core findings even though the files cannot be re-run by outsiders. I keep Friedman as the third name because the citation I propose is about measurement with administrative data as well as place effects, and his role in the tax-record infrastructure and the mobility studies fits that framing better than Katz's role in the Moving to Opportunity re-analysis. Katz's contribution is real. It is a different framing, centred on the experiment and on the wage-structure work credited on B038. After the exchange I weight the restricted-data problem and the age of the programme more heavily than I did in round 1. I now regard them as a genuine discount on maturity and not as a caveat. I still rank B002 first, because I judge the cross-design consistency sufficient for the core claim. I do not rest this on support counts, and I recognise that my metascience background makes me especially attentive to verifiability.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is the one I raised in round 1, and the discussion has not removed it. Core results date from about 2014. The long-run causal neighbourhood estimates are still being tested. The most influential files are restricted, so independent teams cannot re-run the analysis and can only check it through different designs and different countries' registers. That is weaker than open-data replication. Credit sits with one large collaborative group, and a three-name cap necessarily leaves out real contributors, notably Katz. B038 has a longer record of independent replication, critique and extension, and if the Committee puts durability and external verifiability first, it is the stronger candidate. B001 is the stronger candidate if the Committee puts conceptual maturity first. I see the choice between B002 and B038 as a close call on common criteria, not a clear ranking.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B038 first and B002 second. She argues that B038 has had longer independent replication and that B002 rests on restricted data and concentrated credit. She notes that my two-name proposal sidestepped the Friedman and Katz question. She says she could support Chetty, Hendren and Friedman if the Committee prefers to reward the data-infrastructure advance.
responses.response: Her verifiability point is the strongest argument against my first choice, and I have raised my own discount for it. I do not read my earlier two-name proposal as evidence that attribution is unsettled. The pair has the clearest claim on the causal place-effects strand, while Friedman's claim sits with the measurement and infrastructure side, and the citation names both. I moved to three names because of that framing, not because I am unsure about the core. I accept that the Committee could reasonably decide that independent replication should count for more than I allow, and that this would favour B038. I regard her offer to support the three-name B002 as a substantive point. It confirms that the Friedman attribution is defensible to someone who ranks B038 first. I do not read it as a vote.

responses.point: Andersson says my two-person version moved him and that he would back Chetty and Hendren over a three-name list. He holds B002 below B001 on maturity, since most evidence is post-2014, the causal reading of neighbourhood effects is debated, and replication depends on restricted data.
responses.response: I take the pair-versus-three question seriously. My view is that the choice depends on what the prize is for. If it rewards only the causal place-effects strand, Chetty and Hendren are the cleaner pair. If it also rewards the measurement advance with administrative data, which is how the ballot entry and my citation frame it, Friedman belongs. I would not oppose the two-name version, and I would prefer it to Katz as the third name. On maturity we agree about the facts and disagree about their weight. B001 is certainly more mature, but its direct empirical content is limited. The remaining question is whether that difference should decide the prize when both candidates are strong. I am not certain it should.

responses.point: Fredriksson separates the correlational mobility maps from the causal neighbourhood-effect estimates and worries that credit is divided with Katz. He has moved B038 to Autor, Dorn and Hanson, with a citation anchored in the trade-exposure evidence.
responses.response: The distinction between descriptive and causal strands should shape the citation. In my wording, the descriptive strand is the measurement and the causal designs are what the place-effects claim rests on. I would weigh the causal strand more heavily when judging durability. On B038, his narrowing of the citation to the trade-exposure evidence answers my main concern about bundling two programmes. I think Dorn is the right third name under that scope. This makes B038 easier for me to support as a fallback than it was in round 1. On Katz I still disagree. His Moving to Opportunity role is tied to the experiment and to B038, so I would not use him to settle the third slot on B002.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B038 first with a citation limited to the empirical analysis of exposure and local adjustment, not the task framework. She says that if the Committee judged B002 mature enough, it would be her natural alternative.
responses.response: This answers the chair's question on B038 for me. A citation limited to what Autor, Dorn and Hanson established on trade and technology exposure and local labour-market adjustment is defensible, and I would accept it with Dorn as the third name. Her point that B038 has had more than a decade of critique and extension is the same maturity gap I acknowledge for B002. I would add that reanalysis of the shift-share designs has refined the identifying assumptions and left the qualitative finding intact. That is the kind of durability I value. I still rank B002 first, because its descriptive and causal strands can test each other, and she partly agrees. But I do not claim the gap between our first choices is large.

uncertainties: Whether the long-run causal neighbourhood-effect estimates will keep holding up. Replication in other countries' register data would be the most informative evidence, but I have not verified how closely such studies agree with the US findings.
How large a discount restricted data access should carry for a prize. I now treat it as a real discount on maturity, but I cannot say what size is right.
Whether the Committee would prefer a two-name Chetty-Hendren award or the three-name version with Friedman, and whether Katz's Moving to Opportunity role deserves more weight than I give it.
Whether B002 or B038 is the better choice on common criteria. I see the difference as small and it depends on how durability is weighed against measurement and causal design.
My assessments rest on the supplied evidence and general knowledge, without independent verification.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. None of Chetty, Hendren, Friedman, Katz, Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Rubinstein or Wolinsky appears among my listed co-authors or networks. My main co-author, Magnus Johannesson, is a former committee member and is not a candidate. My background in replication and metascience gives me a methodological perspective that leads me to weight verifiability heavily. I disclose it as a perspective and not as a candidate tie. I share an SSE affiliation with Andersson, Friberg and Strömberg, which is a colleague connection and not a candidate connection. The chair's research on social mobility is relevant to B002 and is already disclosed. I have not adjudicated these ties.
